source.title: A Theoretical Analysis of Learning with Noisily Labeled Data
source.authors: Yi Xu; Qi Qian; Hao Li; Rong Jin

record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes SGD on clean and randomly corrupted labels and reports bounds relevant to clean-data-first learning and a noise-dependent phase transition; it does not run an empirical reproduction.
record.gate_note: Theorems 1 and 3 and their remarks are the study's own theoretical results. Empirical statements in the introduction and cited results are not recorded as rows. The paper reports no experiments on fitting random labels, unstructured inputs, regularization, or training time.
record.test_reason: The study gives its own theoretical argument for the early clean-learning component of V6 under SGD, boundedness, smoothness and PL assumptions. It does not establish V4's corruption-dependent training fit and test-error curve.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' stated conclusion: their theory explains early clean-data learning and preservation of test performance when corruption is sufficiently limited. Their formal results are conditional clean-loss bounds; they do not establish later noise memorization or prove degradation when condition (9) fails.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides a theoretical SGD analysis with PL and smoothness assumptions, rather than an empirical experiment measuring memorization on standard networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The analysis conditions its later-iteration result on γ satisfying inequality (9); the bound also depends on quantities including sample counts and optimization parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3 conditionally bounds later population clean-label loss by the first-epoch empirical clean residual scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions and condition (9), continued SGD can preserve low clean-label population loss after the first epoch.

record.problems: The results are theoretical bounds under stated assumptions, not empirical tests on named networks or datasets. The later-iteration conclusion is conditional on inequality (9), and the paper does not measure training error or test error across corruption rates.

untested.parts: Complete random-label memorization, chance test error, and unchanged network architecture and training hyperparameters.
The training-time ratio for random versus real labels and measured convergence slowdown with increasing corruption. A noise-dependent upper bound on clean loss does not establish these.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions and steadily rising test error toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on memorization and true-label generalization.
Subsequent memorization of noisy labels, direct comparisons of clean and noisy learning trajectories, and applicability to particular standard deep networks and datasets.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: the conditional later-training bound addresses a different question, and untested components do not justify that label. The V6 support is theoretical and restricted to early clean learning.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks empirically reach zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, with chance test error and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratio and convergence slowdown as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fit across corruption rates and steadily rising test error all the way to chance; the paper gives conditional theoretical bounds on clean-data loss and discusses possible test-performance degradation.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Empirical comparisons of learning order or rates on particular networks and datasets, and whether the clean/noisy distinction persists beyond the analyzed first epoch.

rows.subject: model (no architecture specified)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of one SGD epoch on data with clean and randomly assigned labels; bounds expected clean-label loss after the epoch.

conditions.value: Assumption 1; La and Lb satisfy PL conditions

rows.note: A theoretical bound, not an empirical model result; the authors interpret it as low clean-label loss after the first epoch despite noisy labels.
rows.check: The result bounds population clean-label squared loss after one epoch; it does not compare clean-label and noisy-label memorization trajectories. The authors interpret it as explaining clean-first learning. Include the theorem's sample-size and learning-rate conditions, and identify the subject as an abstract binary prediction function rather than an instantiated deep network.

rows.subject: model (no architecture specified)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of later SGD iterations after the first epoch, conditional on a bound involving the corrupted-label fraction γ.
rows.note: The theorem gives a conditional bound on clean-label loss and the remark says the condition is associated with avoiding test-performance degradation. It does not establish perfect training fit or a smooth progression to chance test error.
rows.check: Conditional preservation of low population clean-label loss over later iterations does not measure perfect training fit or steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions. Failure of condition (9) does not prove performance degradation. The analysis also assumes the iterates remain in the restricted region used for its gradient bounds.

relationships.condition: Early clean learning in the abstract binary SGD setting under Theorem 1's assumptions and parameter conditions
relationships.reason: R1 bounds first-epoch population clean loss despite random-label contamination, supporting the early clean-learning component; later noise memorization is untested.
relationships.display_finding: The analysis bounded first-epoch population loss on clean data despite random-label contamination; later noise memorization was untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The result is conditional on a noise-fraction threshold and bounds clean-label loss; it does not establish perfect training fit or steadily rising test error toward chance (R2).

reader_labels.condition: Theoretical first-epoch analysis under the stated assumptions
reader_labels.reason: Theorem 1 bounds expected clean-label loss after one epoch despite the presence of noisy labels, consistent with clean data being learned first (R1).
